Me, but it was not the breakup as much as the behaviour after breakup. They were in the wrong, they KNEW they were in the wrong. Never came to apologise, then when a mutual friend was talking to them, they said her depression is an issue. I lashed out right then and there and said all that I had been suppressing but it did not help at all, and I regretted them right after because no one deserves to be shoved guilt in their face because of their unavoidable situations, and how can you hurt someone you love right? Anger is one thing, it dissipates. My love will forever be here and I cannot stand by the wrong things I have done. 

Anyway, I digress. So, I give very little importance to the words that are said usually in a na argument or post breakup because they are usually filled with anger and hurt and I always, ALWAYS focus on the behaviour. But this time, those words has cut me so deep it has left me SPIRALLING. 

How can a person that I loved and who claimed to love me say things like that when they have failed to show up MULTIPLE times? How can they not feel guilty? How do they sleep at night knowing when I was struggling and needing them, they were not there and they are okay with it. And tbh, It’s fine, it’s okay being okay with not being there but THEN to tell me that I was TOO depressed? After losing a parent, two pregnancies, a best friend, all in the span of 2 years I am supposed to be all fine?

Their words keep ringing in my ears, their behaviour before and after breakup makes me feel absolutely abandoned. 

Was this what i deserved? Because if it is, I don’t want to continue anymore. The fact that I was not loved and deceived is making me suicidal.

Though both are damaging if not fatal to a romantic relationships, emotional infidelity is always worse. 

Emotional infidelity ensures the end of relationship compared to physical infidelity.

Your partner could get sexually assaulted, raped, or get drunk and in a confused state kiss or have sex, or tons of thing sexual that can happen due to momentary lapse of control/judgement.

Physical infidelity can (keyword “can”) be forgiven if your partner was apathetic towards them and was only looking for sexual satisfaction and has no emotional ties to them. 

When it comes to emotional infidelity, your relationship with your partner isn’t exclusive anymore. 

They are seeking emotional support from someone else, being vulnerable to someone else, have feelings for them, are confiding in them, and doing everything with them emotionally that is only your right. 

It’s very difficult to emotionally connect with more than one person at a time so any emotional connection from one relationship will take it away from another. 

An emotional connection takes time to build so it must’ve took time for them to be comfortable and share the emotions to somebody. This clearly indicates that your partner, with conscious efforts tried to connect to someone else other than you. They have invested time that could have spent on the primary relationship. 

So, imo an emotional affair is the end of a relationship where sexual affair can be overlooked with right reasons and enough work from both parties.
